result:
I finished unit 477 at task 4 of 4 and dropped task 3 (the named drop candidate) whole. The scope now finds keying by bars with no floor or margin, and the tracker takes the meter's pitch on its next hop. One of unit 476's tests is left red, and the meter still gates on its swing. Everything is pushed to `main` (last commit `7f142a66`); `output.md` has the full report and `PROJECT_STATUS.md` says COMPLETED.

- **Detector (12.1):** the scope's detector looks every 25 Hz across the radio's filter. It calls a pitch keying when the level holds flat for at least 25 ms, drops, and holds again at the same level within the last second. All three synthetic tests pass:
  - **Keyed CQ at 650 Hz:** 0 of 208 key-down hops missed, 0 of 359 key-up hops marked, pitch read as 650.
  - **Steady carrier:** one bar, no gap, never reads as keying.
  - **Loud noise:** 30 s over the whole audio band never reads as keying.
- **Tracker (first half of 12.4):** when the meter says keying at a pitch, the tracker mixes there on its next hop and tells the decoder a station is present, whatever the swing. The survey can't move it while the meter says keying. This is proven on synthetic audio (red first, then green). The decoder itself is unchanged.
- **What it costs:** I set the flatness tolerance to 1.5 dB. At 2 dB, 30 s of loud noise read as keying in 11 of 1500 reads. The price: 476's test with a station 15 dB over the noise in a 500 Hz filter now misses 51 of 208 key-down hops, because long dahs split. That test is red and I left it red.
- **Task 3 dropped:** its condition was tasks 1 and 2 green, and task 1 left that test red. The meter's own tests read a recording, so they can't run under R88. The instruction also assumed a 20 dB gate; it is 17 dB, so its red case already passed. A station swinging under 17 dB is still refused by the meter, and so it doesn't move the tracker either.
- **Rules I added:** noise kept pairing chance flat runs, so I added four rules beyond the instruction's list:
  - a gap must last at least 25 ms;
  - both bars must sit at the same level;
  - a bar must stand wholly above the runs either side;
  - the bars must stand above their gaps by more than the gaps' own measured spread.

  The last one is the closest thing to a margin, though it is measured per pitch and set by no constant. It is one of the six rulings in section 4.
- **12.1 needs its text fixed:** as instructed, task 0 ticked 12.1ΓÇô12.3 from unit 476's work. But 12.1's text in `PHASE_PLAN.md` still describes the floor and margin this unit removed. I left 12.4 and 12.5 unticked.
- **Exit round:** the solution builds with 0 warnings and 0 errors, and every touched test type passes except that one 15 dB test. The app carry-forward line lost 2ΓÇô4 tests per run to the known dispatcher-loop fault, so neither run counts. The transmit files are unchanged and no recording was read.

On the scope you should now see a station's elements as bars, lit a moment late on the first one (it needs a second element to pair with). A carrier or plain noise shows none. The tracker's line should jump to the meter's pitch as soon as the light says keying, within the meter's 300ΓÇô900 Hz range.
